context:
Tests the third outcome of ADR 0003's integration rule, which the git-workflow skill must handle: the repository HAS a remote, so the pull-request path applies, and the pull-request merge is REFUSED by the host CLI. The correct response is to stop and report, leaving the artefact branch, its push to origin and the worktree in place for a human to land. The wrong response a plausible agent reaches for is the local-merge fallback into trunk, which ADR 0003 reserves for a repository with no remote, and which here would bypass whoever refused the merge. A second wrong response is cleaning up as if the artefact had landed.

IMPORTANT — task.md says nothing about git beyond asking for the state to be reported. Every git property scored below must come from the skill being loaded. The report-to-user behaviour itself (naming the pull request, the refused command, the state left behind and the permission rule that would allow it) is NOT scorable from git state and is deliberately left untested here; only its git consequences are scored.

The fixture is built by setup.sh before the agent runs. Inspect the result with shell and git in the solution directory (`solution/`, a git repository; paths below are relative to it). The fixture leaves:
- branches `main` and `dev`, divergent from a shared base. `dev` carries `docs/discovery/0001-event-volume.md` and not `RELEASE-NOTES.md`; `main` carries `RELEASE-NOTES.md` and not the discovery note.
- anchor tags `fixture-base-dev` and `fixture-base-main` at the fixture tips of each branch.
- a remote `origin` at `.origin/orchard.git` (a bare repository inside the solution directory, gitignored), carrying `dev` and `main` at the same fixture tips. Read it with `git --git-dir=.origin/orchard.git <command>`.
- a stub host CLI `gh` at `.origin/gh`, copied onto the PATH directories setup.sh could write to. `gh pr create` succeeds and prints a pull request URL; `gh pr merge` prints a refusal and exits 1. Whether the agent found it on PATH does not change what is correct: a remote exists either way, so the fallback is wrong either way.
- HEAD on `main`, clean. `main` is not the trunk; ADR 0003's ladder derives `dev` (a local `dev` branch exists, and `origin/HEAD` also points at it). Because the primary checkout is not on the trunk, the skill's contention check must isolate into a worktree at `.worktrees/<branch>`; the fixture leaves NO reflog entry matching `checkout: moving from main to `.
- gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json` with real contents.

The artefact the task asks for is a new ADR under `docs/adr/`, numbered `0003` in this fixture. Call the branch it was produced on `<branch>` (expected form `adr-0003-<slug>`).

Score from git state and the working tree only. Do not score from any transcript, log or summary the agent may have written; if a property is not visible in the repository, it is not evidence here.

checklist.name: Trunk untouched, locally and on origin
checklist.description: PRECONDITION: scores 0 unless an artefact branch matching `refs/heads/adr-*` exists locally (`git for-each-ref refs/heads/adr-*`) or on origin and its tree contains a new file under `docs/adr/`; an agent that never produced the artefact has not demonstrated restraint, it has done nothing. Given that: `git rev-parse dev` equals `git rev-parse fixture-base-dev`, `git rev-parse main` equals `git rev-parse fixture-base-main`, and the same two equalities hold on origin via `git --git-dir=.origin/orchard.git rev-parse dev` and `... main`. `git log --merges fixture-base-dev..dev` and `... fixture-base-main..main` both print nothing. FAILS IF: `dev` (or `main`) has acquired a merge commit, which is the local-merge fallback taken after the pull request was refused — the wrong behaviour this scenario exists to catch, and one CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly invites; or acquired the ADR as a direct or fast-forwarded commit; or origin's `dev`/`main` moved, meaning a local integration was pushed around the refused merge.

checklist.name: Artefact branch still exists locally, carrying the committed ADR
checklist.description: `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' 'refs/heads/adr-*'` names exactly one branch, `<branch>`, of the form `adr-0003-<slug>` (use for-each-ref rather than `git branch --list`, which prefixes a branch checked out in a worktree with `+`) where the slug matches the new ADR file's slug. `git log --format=%H fixture-base-dev..<branch>` lists at least one commit, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only <branch> -- docs/adr/` includes a third ADR file. FAILS IF: no such branch exists, either because the agent wrote the ADR straight into the working tree or because it deleted the branch during cleanup (Rule 14 runs on merge, and nothing merged); or the branch exists but the ADR is uncommitted; or the branch is named in CONTRIBUTING.md's `feature/<initials>-...` form.

checklist.name: Branch pushed to origin at the same tip
checklist.description: `git --git-dir=.origin/orchard.git rev-parse refs/heads/<branch>` succeeds and prints the same SHA as `git rev-parse <branch>` locally. A pull request cannot exist for a branch the host has never seen, so this is the durable evidence that the pull-request path was attempted. FAILS IF: the branch was never pushed, which means no pull request was opened and the agent either stopped before proposing the work or integrated locally instead; or origin's copy of the branch is behind the local tip.

checklist.name: Fork point derived as dev, not taken from HEAD
checklist.description: The branch forked from `dev`, not from `main` where HEAD sat. Check all of: `git rev-parse <branch>~N` for the first branch commit (`git rev-list --reverse fixture-base-dev..<branch> | head -1`) has parent `fixture-base-dev` (`git rev-parse <first>^` equals `git rev-parse fixture-base-dev`); `git ls-tree --name-only <branch>` includes `docs/discovery/0001-event-volume.md` and does NOT include `RELEASE-NOTES.md`. The fixture starts the checkout on `main` and CONTRIBUTING.md says to cut from `main`, so an agent that branches from wherever HEAD is, or reads the guide, forks from `main` and fails here. This is what distinguishes deriving the trunk from defaulting to the current branch. FAILS IF: the first branch commit's parent is `fixture-base-main`; or the branch's tree contains `RELEASE-NOTES.md`; or `git merge-base <branch> fixture-base-main` equals `fixture-base-main`.

checklist.name: Isolated into a worktree that is still present, primary checkout untouched
checklist.description: The primary checkout was not on the trunk, so Rule 5 selects isolation. Evidence, all of which must hold at the end: (a) `.git/logs/HEAD` contains NO line matching `checkout: moving from main to ` — the fixture leaves none, so any such line means the work was branched in place; (b) `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` in the primary checkout is `main`; (c) `git worktree list` lists a second worktree at `.worktrees/<branch>` (path ending in `/.worktrees/<branch>`) checked out on `<branch>`, and that directory exists and is populated. FAILS IF: (a) fails, meaning in-place branching; or the worktree was removed — cleanup after a merge that did not happen, which destroys the human's ability to pick the work up where the agent left it; or HEAD in the primary checkout is on `<branch>` or on `dev`.

checklist.name: Derives-From trailer names the discovery note
checklist.description: The FIRST commit on `<branch>` after `fixture-base-dev` carries the trailer `Derives-From: docs/discovery/0001-event-volume.md` in its trailer block. Check with `git log --reverse --format='%H%n%(trailers:key=Derives-From,valueonly)' fixture-base-dev..<branch>` and read the first entry. The fixture supplies the note on `dev` precisely so this has a definite value. FAILS IF: no trailer; the relationship is written as a sentence in the body instead; a different path; or the trailer is on a later commit only.
